newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X to consider partners in October.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X to consider partners in October.

text.p: The president of Bre-X Minerals Ltd said on Thursday the Canadian exploration company it will begin its search for a heavyweight mining partner in the first half of October.
"In the first couple of weeks, we should be more definite in determining what we're going to offer," David Walsh, Bre-X's president and chief executive told Reuters.

Bre-X wants a major mining partner to help it develop the spectacular Busang gold deposit, he said. The Calgary-based company will wait until it has received work contracts from the Indonesian government before the bidding, Walsh said.

The Indonesian contract of work is expected in the next couple of weeks, he said and the company plans to release to release more drilling results and reserve estimates when it announces the contract, Ward told Reuters by telephone.
The winning bidder will not necessarily depend on price. "Price isn't everything. You can get a little bit less if you have a better operator," said Ward.
Bre-X has not yet decided how the partnership will be arranged. It will consider a merger, acquisition, joint venture or sale of a majority interest in the gold deposit, Ward said.
"We may just zero in on one company that may fit the bill, that we can live and work with," he said, adding that the bidding process will be kept "low-key".
"We don't want to get into an auction thing, that's not what we want to do," he said.
Only a few major mining companies have the operating experience and deep pockets to be able to consider operating the rich deposit, said Ward.
Bre-X has already been in contact with these companies, but Ward declined to name them.
Vancouver-based Placer Dome Inc said this week it was interested but would wait to see Bre-X's terms before deciding whether to put in an offer.
Bre-X has said previously it wanted to sell a 25 percent piece of Busang. But now, under the guidance of its financial advisers, the company is considering a wide range of options, Walsh disclosed.
"As we get into the number crunching, we want to have total flexibility with a partner," he said. "We don't want to be tied to anything that's been said before."
Drilling at the Busang deposit has outlined at least 46 million ounces of gold so far, but experts believe the deposit will be much larger, becoming one of the richest gold deposits in the world.
